title: The actual pro-etale open counit under scalar extension
statement:
Fix a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ and a prime $\ell\ne p$. All schemes are separated of finite type over $k$, and all maps are $k$-morphisms [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $\varphi:A\to B$ be a unital homomorphism of finite commutative rings killed by powers of $\ell$, and choose $N=\ell^n\geq1$ annihilating both. On either the ordinary etale or pro-etale site let $\mathcal C_{T,R}=D^b_{ctf}(T,R)$ mean the full category of constant-$R$ module complexes with bounded constructible cohomology and finite Tor amplitude: tensor with any degree-zero module sheaf has cohomology in one fixed finite interval [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf, def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude, det-sp-et-proet-adjunction-transfer]. Write $T_T=-\otimes^L_{A_T}B_T$ [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor, lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. The finite Tate line is $R_T(1)=\mu_{N,T}\otimes_{(\mathbf Z/N)_T}R_T$ on the etale site and its comparison inverse image on the pro-etale site; $(d)$ denotes tensor with its $d$th tensor power [def-asd-finite-etale-tate-twist].
Let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be a quasi-compact open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. On pro-etale finite-Tor categories write $J_R=Dj_{!,R}$ for exact extension by zero, $U_R=j_R^*$ for exact restriction, and $v_R:J_RU_R\to1$ for the degreewise open sum/evaluation counit [def-weil-extension-by-zero, def-weil-proetale-inverse-image, det-sf-mate-open-restriction]. Let $b_j:T_XJ_A\xrightarrow{\sim}J_BT_U$ be the compact-support comparison of [det-sp-reduction-direct-image], identified with open extension via the identity proper factor and then any common-refinement comparison. Let $a_j:T_UU_A\xrightarrow{\sim}U_BT_X$ be the canonical scalar/restriction comparison [def-sp-constant-scalar-pullback-comparison]. Then $J_R\dashv U_R$ on the stated categories is identified, including its actual counit, with transport of the ordinary etale sum adjunction by the specified comparison $\nu_X^*Dj_!^{et}\simeq Dj_!^{pro}\nu_U^*$ [def-sp-fixed-compact-support-comparison]. Under these identifications, for $M\in\mathcal C_{X,A}$,
$$v_{B,T_XM}\circ J_B(a_{j,M})\circ b_j(U_AM)=T_X(v_{A,M}).$$
In particular the right mate of $b_j^{-1}$ is exactly $a_j$ for the specified pro-etale open adjunction. The assertion includes compatibility of both the counit and the left map with the etale/pro-etale identifications, and imposes no flatness assumption on the coefficient map.

proof.text: Put $C_T^R=\nu_T^*$ and use superscripts $e,p$ for the two sites. Finite-type schemes over a field are Noetherian, and finite rings are Noetherian, so the finite-Tor comparison equivalence applies. Given $M\in\mathcal C_{X,A}$ choose $K\in\mathcal C^e_{X,A}$ and $C_X^AK\simeq M$. Choose a bounded flat representative $P$ of $K$ by the finite-coefficient input-model lemma. Its scalar extensions and site pullbacks are K-flat bounded flat representatives, even when $B/A$ is not flat. Restriction carries the finite constructible stratification to its intersections with $U$; the ringed pullback theorem carries $P$ to a K-flat flat representative on $U$. Apply the compact-support-domain lemma to $j$ with identity proper factor to see that $J_R^e$ preserves the finite-Tor constructible subcategories and that all scalar-extended inputs used below remain bounded. The same follows on the pro-etale side by the specified site comparison. Thus the open adjunctions below restrict to the full categories in the statement.

source.place: Locality, with finite-Tor domains from Stacks more-etale.tex, remark-Rf-lower-shriek-change-of-rings

proof.text: On the etale site the extension/restriction adjunction has counit induced on each extension summand by $s\mapsto s$; on an object with no factorization through $U$ its source is zero. On the pro-etale site the defined sheafified extension by zero is likewise the exact left adjoint of restriction. Indeed, a map from its presheaf to $H$ is precisely a compatible family of maps $F(V\to U)\to H(V\to X)$; sheafification extends it uniquely. Taking $F=j^*H$ and the identity family gives the actual pro-etale counit $v_R^p$, with this same evaluation formula. Exact extension and restriction induce degreewise adjunctions on complexes. Their units and counits descend through localization: the two triangle identities are identities of chain maps, and localization preserves their compositions. The resulting counits are therefore precisely $v_R^e,v_R^p$, rather than separately chosen transformations.

source.place: Tags 03DI, 03DJ: lemma-extension-by-zero, lemma-extension-by-zero-exact; their degreewise localization

proof.text:
Write $e_R:C_X^RJ_R^e\simeq J_R^pC_U^R$ for the specified open site comparison and $r_R:C_U^RU_R^e\simeq U_R^pC_X^R$ for the canonical restriction comparison. Its unit normalization is
$$U_R^p(e_R)\circ r_R(J_R^e-)\circ C_U^R(\eta_R^e)=\eta_R^p C_U^R.$$
For an etale complex $H$, transpose $h=C_X^R(v_{R,H}^e)\circ e_R(U_R^eH)^{-1}$ under the actual pro-etale open adjunction. Substitution of this unit identity gives
$$U_R^p(h)\circ\eta_R^p
=U_R^pC_X^R(v_R^e)\circ r_R(J_R^eU_R^eH)\circ C_U^R(\eta_R^e)
=r_R(H),$$
the last equality being naturality of $r_R$ and $U_R^e(v_R^e)\circ\eta_R^e U_R^e=1$. Hence
$$v_{R,C_X^RH}^p\circ J_R^p(r_R(H))\circ e_R(U_R^eH)=C_X^R(v_{R,H}^e).$$
This is first an equality on sheaves and then on complexes and their localizations by Step 2. For the identity proper factor, the fixed compact-support site comparison is exactly $e_R$: its proper counit mate is the identity, and the definition retains the open comparison. The finite-Tor equivalence of Step 1 therefore identifies the transported etale adjunction, including its counit, with the actual pro-etale one. This also fixes the counit intended by the adjunction-transfer statement.

source.place: Tag 09AF, lemma-jshriek-comparison; unit-normalized comparison and explicit counit calculation

proof.text:
Consider first the identity-factor compactification of $j$ on the etale site. An open immersion is etale; it is separated of finite type here because it is quasi-compact and the ambient schemes are Noetherian. The etale-sum normalization clause of the coefficient-compatibility lemma identifies its specified compact-support coefficient map $\beta_j$ with the summandwise map $t_j:T_X^eJ_A^e\simeq J_B^eT_U^e$. On the bounded flat representative $P$ of Step 1, restriction and extension by zero are the degreewise functors, and $J_A^eU_A^eP$ is K-flat by the open scalar/site lemma applied to the restricted bounded flat complex. Thus all tensors in the following equation compute derived scalar extension. Let $a_j^e$ be the inverse of the etale scalar/pullback isomorphism in [def-pur-etale-scalar-pullback-iso]. Its prescribed K-flat restriction comparison retains $s\otimes b$. On an extension summand both composites send $s\otimes b$ to $s\otimes b$ in $(P\otimes_A B)(V)$; on an empty summand both are zero. These maps respect balancing and restrictions, so the equality descends through sheafification and degreewise localization. We obtain
$$v_{B,T_X^eK}^e\circ J_B^e(a_{j,K}^e)\circ\beta_j(U_A^eK)=T_X^e(v_{A,K}^e).$$

source.place: Locality: extension by zero commutes with coefficient extension; integral evaluation calculation

proof.text:
Set $\delta_T:T_T^pC_T^A\simeq C_T^BT_T^e$. For $L\in\mathcal C^e_{U,A}$ the coefficient/site square, specialized to the identity-factor compactification, is
$$J_B^p(\delta_U)\circ b_j(C_U^AL)\circ T_X^p(e_A(L))
=e_B(T_U^eL)\circ C_X^B(\beta_j(L))\circ\delta_X(J_A^eL).$$
In particular this compares the named $b_j$, not an arbitrary tensor isomorphism. The scalar/pullback cube, specialized to $j$ and inverted in its pullback comparisons, gives
$$U_B^p(\delta_X(K))\circ a_{j,C_X^AK}^p\circ T_U^p(r_A(K))
=r_B(T_X^eK)\circ C_U^B(a_{j,K}^e)\circ\delta_U(U_A^eK).$$
Here $a_j^p$ is exactly the inverse of the $\lambda_j$ of the stated scalar/restriction definition: both use the same constant-ring maps and balanced K-flat comparison. The cube has no flatness hypothesis. All its inversions are inversions of canonical pullback or tensor isomorphisms, not inversions of counits.

source.place: Locality: identification of the specified left and right scalar maps through the etale/pro-etale comparisons

proof.text:
For clarity the cancellation proving the desired pro-etale equation is as follows. Put $L=U_A^eK$ and
$$D=T_X^p\bigl(J_A^p(r_A(K))\circ e_A(L)\bigr):T_X^pC_X^AJ_A^eL\xrightarrow{\sim}T_X^pJ_A^pU_A^pC_X^AK.$$
Precompose the asserted equation at $C_X^AK$ by $D$ and postcompose by $\delta_X(K)$. Naturality of $b_j$ moves $T_X^pJ_A^p(r_A)$ across $b_j$; the first square of Step 5 replaces $J_B^p(\delta_U)b_jT_X^p(e_A)$, and its second square replaces $U_B^p(\delta_X)a_j^pT_U^p(r_A)$. Naturality of $v_B^p$ moves $\delta_X(K)$ through the counit. The result for the left side is
$$C_X^B\bigl(v_B^e\circ J_B^e(a_j^e)\circ\beta_j(U_A^eK)\bigr)\circ\delta_X(J_A^eU_A^eK),$$
using naturality of $e_B$ and the counit equation of Step 3 over $B$. For the right side, Step 3 over $A$ followed by naturality of $\delta_X$ gives
$$C_X^B(T_X^e(v_A^e))\circ\delta_X(J_A^eU_A^eK).$$
Step 4 equates these. Cancel the invertible $D$ and $\delta_X(K)$ to obtain the required equation at $C_X^AK$. Naturality along $C_X^AK\simeq M$ proves it at the original $M$.

source.place: Locality: pasting the explicit counit and coefficient comparison equations of Steps 3--5

proof.text: The refinement equality of the coefficient-compatibility lemma identifies $b_j$ for every common-refinement comparison with the one just computed using the identity proper factor. Conjugating Step 6 by these fixed identifications preserves the equation; the counits remain those of Step 3. Finally the mate definition says that the transpose of the right mate of $b_j^{-1}:J_BT_U\to T_XJ_A$ is $T_X(v_A)\circ b_j(U_A-)^{-1}$. Step 6, composed with $b_j(U_A-)^{-1}$, says exactly that this transpose is $v_B\circ J_B(a_j)$. Injectivity of the adjunction bijection identifies that mate with $a_j$. The argument includes zero summands, zero complexes, identity opens and empty opens; it used bounded flat representatives of inputs, never flatness of the coefficient map.
